decisions.reason: As a low-noise improvement to the firm's core infrared heating line, it likely costs little to keep available and still preserves upside in a growing market for efficient building heating.
A gas infrared plaque heater with its own product page signals a meaningful commitment in a core category, so management would likely continue it unless results were clearly weak.

This radiant heater is close to the established offer, but as a more specific variant with weaker visibility than the main products it faces a somewhat higher rationalization risk while still being worth keeping open.

Infrared tube heaters fit the firm's existing capabilities and customer base well, and in B2B machinery markets such platform-based variants are usually kept unless evidence strongly shows low demand.
A standard gas infrared plaque heater broadens coverage of a central product family at low additional uncertainty, making continued offering the most likely choice.

Because it appears to overlap with another gas-fired infrared tube heater, it has the highest chance of portfolio pruning, but the low cost of keeping a core variant available still slightly favors retention.
